parameters.content:
## OWNER RULE: SMALL BATCHES, ALWAYS

"never giant runs - process in small batches, then STOP: test,
look at output together, adjust, run the next batch."

`Loop Over Items` **Batch Size = 10** is a deliberately small
START value, not a throughput target. Tune DOWN before up.
Rate-limit safety AND review cadence in one knob.

Pacing/quota enforcement itself lives in **Portkey** (per-provider
limits), not in n8n counters (Shape-6 ruling).

## EVERY OUTPUT IS A DRAFT BY DESIGN

`classifier_version` rides on every row. Nothing downstream may
treat these labels as authoritative; NOTHING auto-promotes off a
classification alone.

Re-classification must be cheap and TOTAL: bump the version,
re-run the corpus, compare. Old labels are **superseded, not
overwritten**.

Anti-over-flagging: the schema tells the model that low certainty
biases severity LOW. Flagging decisions are NOT made here - they
are made (or refused) in `wf-judge-gate`.

nodes.name: STICKY - Everything here is a DRAFT

parameters.content:
## MODEL CALLS -> SELF-HOSTED PORTKEY (Shape 5)

No Portkey n8n node exists (verified: npm has none). The sanctioned
path is the **native OpenAI Chat Model node pointed at our gateway**:

- Credential **PORTKEY_GATEWAY (placeholder)** of type `openAiApi`
  - Base URL = `{{PORTKEY_BASE_URL}}`  (OUR self-hosted gateway,
    never api.portkey.ai)
  - API Key  = the Portkey key whose attached config is
    `{{PORTKEY_CONFIG_ID}}` (`strategy.mode = loadbalance`,
    targets = NIM / Gemini x4 keys / OpenRouter free / Ollama)
- Model id placeholders: `{{PORTKEY_CLASSIFY_MODEL}}` (cheap tier),
  `{{PORTKEY_FIXER_MODEL}}` (stronger tier).
- n8n will warn "can't validate credential against OpenAI" - expected
  and harmless (confirmed by Portkey staff on the n8n forum).

Rotation across the free pool is the GATEWAY's job. n8n makes ONE call.

## DEVIATION - RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN

The Stage-4 brief asked for **Information Extractor** with an
**Auto-fixing Output Parser wrapped over a Structured Output Parser**.

In n8n 2.36.6 the Information Extractor node accepts **only** a
`ai_languageModel` sub-node - it has no output-parser input and no
"Enable Auto-Fixing" toggle (verified against docs.n8n.io on
2026-08-24; it uses a Structured Output Parser internally).

So both instructions are honoured by splitting them:
1. **Information Extractor (Define using JSON Schema)** = the primary
   pass (native-first rule).
2. On a parse/extract failure its **error output** routes to
   **Repair - Basic LLM Chain**, which DOES carry
   `Auto-fixing Output Parser -> Structured Output Parser` with a
   STRONGER fix-up model. That is exactly the "one LLM-corrected
   retry before failing" Interview B required for free-tier models.

Sub-node gotcha: expressions inside ANY sub-node resolve to the
FIRST item only - never put per-item expressions in the parsers.

nodes.name: STICKY - Extractor vs auto-fixing parser (deviation, read me)

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You label one chunk of a conversation transcript.
Chunk occurred at {{ $json.occurred_at_iso }} (epoch ms {{ $json.occurred_at_epoch_ms }}) - weigh nothing that postdates it.
If you are not certain, choose FEWER labels and a LOWER severity. Under-calling is correct behaviour here; over-flagging is the failure mode we are fixing. Do not speculate beyond the text.

messageValues.message: The primary extractor failed to return schema-valid JSON for this chunk. Re-read the chunk and emit ONLY the required JSON object. If uncertain: fewer labels, lower severity.
